The only time I feel "real" is when I'm high or drunk, because then the world goes fuzzy and I don't have to be this person who nobody wants around.

It hurts so much knowing that I had someone—my boyfriend—who saw me at my absolute worst, in the hospital, and still loved me. He fought for us even when it seemed impossible. And now? Now he's gone, and I'm left with people who can't even handle my vulnerability. It makes me question if I'm actually broken, or if I'm just... invisible. That really made me question if anyone actually *sees* me, or if I'm just a patient who fills their schedule.

When you're in crisis and your counselor isn't there to catch you, it's easy to believe that no one can save you. It makes me feel so alone and like a burden for reaching out. Every time I try to ask for help, I immediately start feeling guilty and unworthy. Do you think maybe I'm making this all out of proportion again? Or is it just that deep down inside, where nobody else can reach me, that I truly am invisible?
